key_insight: MAC is the first public conversion-rate (CVR) dataset that provides conversion labels under multiple attribution mechanisms, enabling multi-attribution learning (MAL) and fair benchmarking across attribution strategies.
problem_solved: Existing public CVR datasets contain labels from a single attribution mechanism, which prevents development and evaluation of models that learn from multiple attribution views; MAC fills this data gap by releasing multi-attribution labels and a standardized benchmark.
method: Assemble a real-world CVR dataset and generate conversion labels under multiple attribution mechanisms (e.g., last-touch, first-touch, time-decay, probabilistic) to provide diverse supervision signals.
Define benchmark tasks and a standardized evaluation protocol that compare single-label and multi-attribution learning approaches across the different labelings.
Evaluate representative MAL and baseline CVR models to quantify performance gains and analyze how different attribution mechanisms affect model behavior.
impact: MAC enables researchers and practitioners to train and compare models that leverage multiple attribution signals, improving robustness and interpretability of CVR prediction and accelerating reproducible research in ad-tech and attribution-aware ML.
visual_elements: Dataset overview card: counts (users, impressions, conversions) and number of attribution labels per conversion
Attribution comparison diagram: same user-ad conversion shown with different labels under multiple attribution rules
Benchmark results heatmap or grouped bar chart: model performance across attribution mechanisms and tasks
Pipeline diagram: data collection → multi-attribution labeling → MAL training → standardized evaluation
paper_title: MAC: A Conversion Rate Prediction Benchmark Featuring Labels Under Multiple Attribution Mechanisms
paper_authors: Jinqi Wu, Sishuo Chen, Zhangming Chan, Yong Bai, Lei Zhang
